activities.caption: order the life the paragraph tells
activities.name: islamProphetOrder

config.prompt: Mecca, Medina, Mecca — order the framework events:
items: A merchant of Mecca, born c. 570
Revelations begin in the cave of Hira during Ramadan — Laylat al-Qadr
Persecution drives the Hijra: migration to Medina, 622, year one of the calendar
The model community built: a constitution, a mosque as civic centre, the umma
Conquest of Mecca (630); Arabia largely unified under the new faith
Death in 632, as religious and political head
config.why: Two frameworks matter for everything after: Muhammad honoured as the final prophet — the 'seal' of a line through Abraham, Moses, David, Jesus — and the sunnah, his reported practice, as model life alongside the Quran.

activities.anchor: Watch how much doctrine hangs on one word
activities.caption: pair each article or root with its content
activities.name: islamArticlesMatch

config.prompt: Sunni Six Articles, Shia Five Roots — pair each term with what it claims:

pairs.right: the absolute oneness of God — shirk is the cardinal sin
God-appointed, infallible head of the community after Muhammad — distinctively Shia
divine justice — God is just in a rationally knowable sense
divine decree — God's omniscience, debated against human responsibility

config.why: Tawhid anchors both lists; the divergence concentrates on who may lead — and on how far God's justice can be read by reason.

activities.anchor: Arabic-speaking Christians use the same word
activities.caption: true or false — the name of God
activities.name: islamAllahJudge

statements.s: 'Allah' is Arabic for 'the God' — not the name of a separate Muslim deity.
statements.why: The misconception treats a translation as a different god; the word names the one God of the Abrahamic line.

statements.s: Christians who speak Arabic call God 'Allah' too.
statements.why: The word is shared across the faiths — the misconception's core claim collapses on contact with this fact.

statements.s: Islam presents itself as introducing a new god rather than continuing the prophetic line.
statements.why: It presents itself as the continuation of a line through Abraham, Moses and Jesus — the Quran confirms (and Muslims hold, corrects) the Torah, Psalms and Gospel.

statements.s: The same Semitic root appears in Syriac 'alaha'.
statements.why: One God, one root, several languages — a reminder that translation history runs through all the Abrahamic vocabulary.

config.prompt: The hajj, once in a lifetime for those able, draws its great season crowd to Mecca. Roughly how many pilgrims?
config.why: Two to three million in the great season — dressed in plain white ihram, kings indistinguishable from the poor, circling the Kaaba seven times and standing on the plain of Arafat.
config.context: The largest regular human assembly on Earth — doctrine made habit, at body scale.

activities.anchor: hold the twelfth imam went into occultation
activities.caption: 632: the succession question — play both answers
activities.name: islamSuccessionBranch

config.root: It is 632. The Prophet has died. The Quran does not settle who leads the community. Two answers will define two branches — step into each:

start.text: The community gathers. Leadership must be decided. Which answer do you follow?

choices.label: Choose a caliph from the community
choices.feedback: The Sunni answer — 'people of the sunnah and consensus': Abu Bakr chosen, then Umar, Uthman, Ali (the 'rightly guided' four).

choices.label: Hold that God appointed Ali and his line
choices.feedback: The Shia answer — 'the party of Ali': leadership falls to the Prophet's cousin and son-in-law, and to his hereditary, divinely-guided line of imams.

sunni.text: The caliphate proceeds — and the majority world of roughly 85–90 per cent of Muslims spans every school and continent today.

shia.text: At Karbala (680) Ali's son Husayn, refusing allegiance to the Umayyad caliph, was killed with his small band — grief-for-justice that still organises Shia identity. Twelver Shia (Iran, Iraq, Bahrain, Lebanon, Azerbaijan — roughly 10–15 per cent of Muslims) await the twelfth imam's return as the Mahdi; Ismailis and Zaydis follow other trajectories.

config.why: Both branches share Quran, Prophet, pillars and law — the split is about succession and authority, not about God. Sufism cuts across both.

activities.caption: find the faulty line — the split surveyed
activities.name: islamSplitSpot

config.prompt: One line of this split-survey is wrong — click it:
lines: Both branches share the Quran, the Prophet, the pillars and the law.
Twelver Shia are roughly 10–15 per cent of Muslims; the Sunni majority is roughly 85–90 per cent.
The split is a theological disagreement about the nature of God — each branch has its own deity.
The division is about succession and authority — who may lead after Muhammad.
Karbala (680) turned a political question into a defining act of mourning.
config.correction: The split is about succession and authority, not about God — both branches share the sources.
config.why: Which is exactly the formulation the lesson asks you to keep precise: leadership, not theology, is the fault line.

activities.anchor: Law then draws on four sources
activities.caption: order the four sources
activities.name: islamSourcesOrder

config.prompt: From text to method — order the four sources of Islamic law:
items: Sunnah — the Prophet's reported practice, verified through isnad
config.why: Through these run the fiqh schools — Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali among Sunnis, Ja'fari among Twelver Shia — living legal methods, not monoliths. Hadith science (isnad: verified chains of transmission) is a historiographical apparatus without ancient parallel.

activities.anchor: makes a living legal tradition look like a code
activities.caption: drag between the path and its application
activities.name: islamShariaCompare

config.prompt: The pair modern debates keep collapsing — drag the divider:

before.label: Sharia — 'the path'
before.text: God's ideal path — named, singular, not contained in any book of rules.

after.label: Fiqh — the application
after.text: The fallible human science of applying it — competing schools with different methods, arguing case by case.

config.why: The jurists' own deep theory, the maqasid al-sharia, reads the law as protecting five goods — religion, life, intellect, lineage and property — a frame modernist jurists use to argue for reform and quietists for continuity.

activities.anchor: the direction of prayer before Mecca
activities.caption: pair each time or place with its role
activities.name: islamSacredMatch

config.prompt: Sacred time and sacred space — pair each with what it does:

pairs.right: breaks the Ramadan fast with a feast and obligatory charity
commemorates Abraham's willingness — sacrifice and meat distributed
Shia mourning for Husayn — a voluntary fast day for Sunnis
the cube traced to Abraham and Ishmael, toward which the qibla points
the third holy city — Al-Aqsa, site of the night journey

config.why: The mosque is the local unit: mihrab niche marking the qibla, minbar pulpit, minaret for the call — and no altar, no clergy of sacramental rank: scholars (ulama) carry interpretive authority, a different kind of hierarchy.
